scenarios.name: Order prediction in an authorized nonproduction serving lab
scenarios.summary: A fictional ML engineer carries one frozen, anonymous two-feature order prediction package through schema checks, online and chunked inference, readiness, reproducible deployment, authorization, bounded service measurements, scaling and approved rollback. All records, artifact sources and runtime observations are authored lab fixtures. No real production results or credentials are asserted.

assets.title: Five keyed orders
assets.description: The glossary specifies unnamed features, not real-world feature semantics. These two anonymous feature names are the declared running contract. The first three rows are the online matrix; all five form the two-two-one batch input. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Synthetic order identity; A and B retain the glossary key example.

columns.name: feature_1
columns.description: First anonymous prediction-time feature, permitted closed interval [0, 10].

columns.name: feature_2
columns.description: Second anonymous prediction-time feature, permitted closed interval [0, 10].

assets.title: Persisted keyed batch results
assets.description: Predictions computed by executing the supplied frozen fixture package; keyed JSONL mirrors these rows. Not an answer for the learner batch procedure. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

planted_issues.description: Authored same count wrong keys fixture.

assets.title: Complete client and handler evidence
assets.description: Probe retains exactly 300 starts in [0,300), with 294 HTTP-200 valid responses inside two seconds, two handled HTTP errors, two external timeouts and two connection refusals. Load rate_10 preserves the glossary 100/90/6/4 ten-second example. Scaling compares two and three replicas at the same offered load. Null completion is not a zero latency. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements. Responses received after the two-second deadline are failed attempts, not successful completions; late response observations do not contribute to successful throughput.

columns.name: http_status
columns.description: HTTP protocol code, not a measured magnitude.

columns.name: terminal_outcome_seconds
columns.description: Client terminal outcome time: response arrival for completed attempts, start plus two seconds for timeouts, start for immediate connection refusal. Late responses remain separate evidence.

assets.title: Backlog observations throughout each measurement
assets.description: Three observations per fixed ten-second window distinguish stable backlog from growth. Timed-out attempts remain failures; unfinished work is an additional boundary observation, not a second category of attempts to sum into the denominator. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements. Client attempts still awaiting a terminal outcome, not queued-only work. Queued-only backlog, if needed, is a separate measure.

columns.name: unfinished_requests
columns.description: Client attempts still awaiting a terminal outcome; request_start_seconds < elapsed_seconds < terminal_outcome_seconds. Queued-only backlog, if needed, is a separate measure.

assets.title: Identified batching trace
assets.description: The first limit_2 observation preserves start 1.0, wait end 1.4, response completion 1.6. Same input identities under two measured limits; failure and unmatched response are explicit edge records. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

assets.title: Authored container-top process snapshots
assets.description: Both snapshots accompany a configured worker limit of two. Supporting supervisor is not a prediction worker; three actual workers expose oversubscription. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

assets.title: Concurrent CPU and memory observations
assets.description: CPU and memory recorded during the matching process/load interval; no CPU-only availability inference is intended. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

assets.title: Original, changed and restored identities
assets.description: Nonproduction lifecycle and replica fixture preserves the original one-replica setting. Identifiers are local fictional fixture labels, not real cloud resources. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

assets.title: Controllable initialization fixtures
assets.description: All partial initialization states are supplied; the learner implements readiness status and JSON handling. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

assets.title: Approval and immutable fixture artifact records
assets.description: Synthetic content-addressed artifact identities are computed from included authored package sources. They are offline fixture references, not remotely pullable production images. A is approved previous; B is faulty test. No latest version selection is authorized. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

assets.title: Rollback ordering fixture
assets.description: Authored reference chronology for before/after visuals; not evidence of commands run on an actual container. All observations are authored nonproduction fixture data, not production measurements.

assets.title: Validate prediction request and response schemas — bounded fixture workspace

files.content:
# Validate prediction request and response schemas

Fictional order-prediction lab; all data and runtime observations are authored fixtures. No credentials, live cloud resources or pullable container images are supplied. The image identities are computed from the included release package bytes. A deployment-capable authorized runtime must bind these fixture identities to its local image/scaffold; these files do not claim deployment occurred.

## Supplied contract
Anonymous feature_1 and feature_2, request key features, output keys predictions and version. These concrete names and limits are authored here because the glossary leaves them unnamed. Read contract.json before using any fixtures.

## Learner task (glossary)
Within supplied infrastructure scaffolding, write a Python function and its required imports to exchange JSON requests and responses against one declared prediction contract. Author reusable fixtures for a valid three-row, two-feature order matrix, an included numeric limit, a value beyond that limit, a missing required key, an incorrect matrix width and an incorrectly aligned response. Validate decoded structures and assert the expected acceptance or rejection of each case.

## Starter-state intent (glossary)
Supply an authorized endpoint and infrastructure scaffolding, plus a contract declaring request and response key names, permitted numeric limits, a two-feature order matrix and output row alignment. Supply no complete client or validation function. Fixture fields use only the supplied contract names, and the learner writes imports, reusable fixtures, transport, checks and assertions.

## Observable success (glossary)
Assertion checks pass for normal and included-limit fixtures. Missing-key, wrong-type, out-of-range, wrong-rank and wrong-width fixtures are explicitly rejected rather than treated as successful predictions. A supplied response with missing output fields or incorrect row alignment fails response validation. The HTTP exchange uses encoded JSON bytes, the required header and a stated timeout.

## Visual intent (glossary)
Make the serialized body, decoded request, required-versus-supplied keys, matrix rank and width, decoded response row alignment, and fixture acceptance or rejection visible alongside the learner's assertion results.

Dataset CSV headers and all records are copied from the registry by the builder. Measurement records are observations, not computed summary answers. Offline infrastructure helpers supply transport/status bytes or recorded outcomes; author the requested imports, logic, fixtures and assertions in learner.py. Runtime commands listed by the glossary are tasks for the authorized fixture environment, not commands this registry builder executes.

## Supplied endpoint
Start `python3 endpoint_scaffold.py` in this workspace. POST URL: `http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict`. The supplied server executes the frozen package and rejects malformed JSON/keys/types/rank/width/bounds with HTTP 400. Learner transport, client validation, reusable fixtures and assertions remain unwritten in learner.py.

{
  "fixture_only": true,
  "domain": "anonymous two-feature orders",
  "feature_names": [
    "feature_1",
    "feature_2"
  ],
  "request_keys": [
    "features"
  ],
  "response_keys": [
    "predictions",
    "version"
  ],
  "matrix_rank": 2,
  "matrix_width": 2,
  "feature_min": 0.0,
  "feature_max": 10.0,
  "limits_inclusive": true,
  "numpy_dtype": "float64",
  "prediction_rows": "one per request row",
  "batch_key": "order_id",
  "batch_result_keys": [
    "order_id",
    "prediction",
    "version"
  ],
  "chunk_size": 2,
  "batch_input_path": "orders.csv",
  "batch_output_path": "learner_results.jsonl",
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": 8080,
  "prediction_route": "/predict",
  "readiness_route": "/ping",
  "success_status": 200,
  "schema_rejection_status": 400,
  "denied_status": 403,
  "not_ready_status": 503,
  "ready_payload": {
    "ready": true
  },
  "not_ready_payload": {
    "ready": false
  },
  "timeout_seconds": 2.0,
  "healthcheck": {
    "command": [
      "CMD",
      "python",
      "health_probe.py"
    ],
    "interval_seconds": 5,
    "timeout_seconds": 2,
    "retries": 3
  },
  "version": "A",
  "expected_request": {
    "features": [
      [
        1.0,
        2.0
      ],
      [
        2.0,
        3.0
      ],
      [
        3.0,
        4.0
      ]
    ]
  },
  "expected_response": {
    "predictions": [
      5.0,
      8.0,
      11.0
    ],
    "version": "A"
  },
  "expected_audience": "order-prediction-fixture",
  "permitted_subjects": [
    "fixture-subject-permitted"
  ],
  "credential_secret_reference": "credential",
  "injected_secret_variable": "ORDER_FIXTURE_CREDENTIAL",
  "logging_policy": "Record failure class only; never record token, credential literal or protected request values."
}

{
  "fixture_only": true,
  "CONFIG_PATH": "compose.yaml",
  "NAME": "prediction",
  "SERVICE": "prediction",
  "INSTANCE": "order-lab",
  "ZONE": "fixture-zone",
  "BRANCH": "verify-order-release",
  "BASE_BRANCH": "main",

  "HOST_PORT": 8080,
  "CONTAINER_PORT": 8080,
  "SETTING": "MODE",
  "VALUE": "fixture",
  "REPLICA_COUNT": 1,
  "worker_limit_key": "WORKER_LIMIT",
  "approved_worker_limit": 2,
  "supported_resource_limits": {
    "cpus": 1.0,
    "memory": "256M"
  },
  "secret_reference": "credential",
  "secret_environment_variable": "ORDER_FIXTURE_CREDENTIAL",
  "supports_deploy_fields": true,
  "original_replica_count": 1,
  "replica_bounds": {
    "min": 1,
    "max": 3
  },
  "original_instance_status": "RUNNING",
  "scaling_policy": {
    "MinCapacity": 1,
    "MaxCapacity": 3,
    "metric": "SageMakerVariantInvocationsPerInstance",
    "target_value": 10.0,
    "scale_in_cooldown_seconds": 60,
    "scale_out_cooldown_seconds": 30
  },
  "authorization": "Only local nonproduction fixture identities and supplied lifecycle/secret hooks; no cloud or registry credentials are bundled."
}

{
  "units": "seconds",
  "ddof": 0,
  "declared_percentile": 99,
  "percentile_method": "linear",
  "probe": {
    "t0": 0.0,
    "window": "[0, 300)",
    "attempt_count": 300,
    "rate_per_second": 1,
    "deadline_seconds": 2.0,
    "earliest_summary_time_seconds": 301.0,
    "error_classification": "Every attempt not HTTP 200 with a valid prediction received within two seconds"
  },
  "load": {
    "offered_rates": [
      5,
      10,
      15
    ],
    "measurement_seconds": 10.0,
    "warmup_seconds": 2.0,
    "arrival_profile": "fixed evenly spaced starts",
    "payload_mix": "valid first-three-order matrix only; intentional malformed fixtures run separately",
    "max_in_flight": 30,
    "timeout_seconds": 2.0,
    "minimum_success_probability": 0.9,
    "maximum_failed_fraction": 0.1,
    "maximum_p99_seconds": 1.0,
    "minimum_successful_throughput_per_second": 5.0,
    "backlog_rule": "No increase between sampled unfinished-work observations; end unfinished work zero"
  },
  "batching": {
    "settings": [
      "limit_1",
      "limit_2"
    ],
    "maximum_p99_seconds": 0.5,
    "population": "Matched successful decoded responses only; exclude failure and unmatched response"
  },
  "scaling": {
    "offered_rate": 10.0,
    "measurement_seconds": 10.0,
    "settings": [
      "replicas_2",
      "replicas_3"
    ],
    "minimum_success_probability": 0.95,
    "maximum_p99_seconds": 1.0,
    "minimum_successful_throughput_per_second": 9.0
  },
  "late_response_policy": "Responses received after the two-second deadline are failed attempts, not successful completions; late response observations do not contribute to successful throughput.",
  "unfinished_requests_definition": "Client attempts still awaiting a terminal outcome: request_start_seconds < elapsed_seconds < terminal_outcome_seconds. Immediate connection refusal terminates at request start; timeout terminates at start plus two seconds. Queued-only backlog, if needed, is a separate measure."
}
# Author the glossary task here, including your imports, functions and assertions.

{
  "allowed_syntax": [
    "import json",
    "import numpy as np",
    "import urllib.request",
    "from urllib.error import HTTPError",
    "def with parameters and return",
    "dictionary, list, string, integer and floating-point literals",
    "variable assignment",
    "for loops over fixtures",
    "if, elif and else",
    "try and except for JSON decoding, array construction and HTTP rejection",
    "set construction and key-set comparisons",
    "isinstance and type checks",
    "comparison operators and boolean predicates",
    "len",
    "dictionary key access and membership checks",
    "json.dumps and json.loads",
    "str.encode and bytes.decode",
    "np.asarray with a declared dtype",
    "NumPy ndim, shape and dtype inspection",
    "NumPy elementwise comparisons and np.all",
    "urllib.request.Request with url, data, headers and method",
    "urllib.request.urlopen with timeout",
    "with context management and response.read",
    "HTTPError.code and HTTPError.read",
    "raise ValueError for explicit schema rejection",
    "assert predicate checks"
  ],
  "blocked_syntax": [
    "model.predict",
    "preprocessing_pipeline.transform",
    "prediction route decorators and endpoint handler definitions",
    "authentication token or credential configuration",
    "readiness endpoint definitions",
    "service telemetry instrumentation",
    "concurrent or asynchronous request execution",
    "load-generation loops",
    "deployment, scaling or rollback client calls"
  ]
}

# Expose model readiness checks before admitting prediction traffic

Fictional order-prediction lab; all data and runtime observations are authored fixtures. No credentials, live cloud resources or pullable container images are supplied. The image identities are computed from the included release package bytes. The executable offline runtime below binds fixture identities to the supplied local prediction packages; it does not claim real Docker/cloud deployment occurred.

## Supplied contract
Anonymous feature_1 and feature_2, request key features, output keys predictions and version. These concrete names and limits are authored here because the glossary leaves them unnamed. Read contract.json before using any fixtures.

## Learner task (glossary)
Implement readiness handling and verification in learner-defined Python functions with learner-written imports, using the supplied container image and its declared contract. Implement do_GET for the readiness route, serialize readiness as JSON, and admit inference only when both the fitted model and preprocessor are initialized and usable. Configure the declared healthcheck, start the named container with its declared port and nonsecret settings, inspect its identity, State and logs, and assert HTTP status and decoded readiness before and after initialization.

## Starter-state intent (glossary)
Supply the referenced image, HTTP server scaffold, declared readiness route, status and JSON contract, healthcheck settings, and controllable fitted model and preprocessor initialization states. Leave the readiness logic, required imports and verification function unwritten. Include fixtures for neither object initialized, each partial-initialization state, successful initialization and initialization failure.

## Observable success (glossary)
Learner-written assertions check both HTTP status and decoded JSON for every declared fixture, including partial initialization and failure. An unready fixture cannot pass the ready assertions. After successful initialization, the endpoint satisfies the declared readiness contract and the configured container healthcheck succeeds. Container inspection confirms image identity and State, and captured logs are checked for initialization or execution failures.

## Visual intent (glossary)
Make the traffic-admission boundary visible through handler state, HTTP status, decoded JSON and container health results: a running process remains non-ready while either fitted object is unavailable, then becomes ready only after both are initialized and usable.

Dataset CSV headers and all records are copied from the registry by the builder. Measurement records are observations, not computed summary answers. Offline infrastructure helpers supply transport/status bytes or recorded outcomes; author the requested imports, logic, fixtures and assertions in learner.py. Runtime commands listed by the glossary are tasks for the authorized fixture environment, not commands this registry builder executes.

## Executable OFFLINE authorized runtime
Run from this workspace. PyYAML is the declared configuration dependency (`import yaml`). Export the runtime secret variable named in runtime_contract.json from an authorized local secret source; no secret literal is supplied or written into configuration/state. Child services inherit this variable only.
1. `python3 offline_runtime.py init` initializes the isolated fixture state (rollback starts only B; worker/scaling start original_config.json; other concepts leave deployment actions to the learner).
2. `python3 offline_runtime.py serve` launches the supplied local endpoint at the HOST_PORT in runtime_contract.json. Use `--name`, `--image`, `--port`, `--case` or `--fault` to select supplied identities/controls. Do not launch a second server on an occupied port.
3. Prefix the concept's declared runtime command with `python3 offline_runtime.py exec`, for example `python3 offline_runtime.py exec docker inspect prediction`. Docker/Compose commands launch and inspect local services; image inspect resolves only fixture release identities. Compose reads the learner's YAML and applies its image/environment/ports/replicas/resources. Replicas use adjacent local host ports. Instance/SSH, autoscaling and repository operations are explicitly simulated local state transitions, never external operations or mutations of the pack repository. Use only commands permitted by constraints.json.
4. `python3 offline_runtime.py state` inspects scoped identity/configuration and configured-healthcheck State.Health; `python3 offline_runtime.py events` shows captured application/inspection/lifecycle ordering. `python3 offline_runtime.py cleanup` terminates only this fixture's child services when finished (harness cleanup, not a learner command).
POST and GET routes are prediction_route and readiness_route from contract.json on `http://127.0.0.1:<HOST_PORT>`. Request timeout is the contract's two seconds. This runtime produces local execution evidence, not production performance measurements. Learner configuration, acceptance assertions, measurements, readiness/authentication logic and verification decisions remain unwritten.

Readiness startup: `python3 server_scaffold.py --case neither --port 8080`, URL `http://127.0.0.1:8080/ping`. Cases: neither, model_only, preprocessor_only, both, initialization_failure. Stop and restart with --case, or call server_scaffold.select_case(case_id) inside the running process. Implement learner.do_GET(handler, initialization_state); handler.reply(status, payload) sends bytes. No readiness predicate or readiness assertions are supplied.

The offline runtime itself needs only standard-library Python on Linux. When PyYAML is unavailable to the harness, its private offline_yaml.py accepts the declared simple mapping/list/scalar configuration subset (including JSON-form YAML). Unsupported YAML forms are explicitly rejected. Learner yaml.safe_dump/yaml.safe_load work still requires the declared PyYAML dependency; the private parser is infrastructure, not a learner solution.

State.Health reports execution of the configured healthcheck, not an unconditional readiness probe.

Implement is_ready(initialization_state), use it in do_GET, and admit inference only when both assets are initialized and initialization has not failed.

# Instrument prediction-service availability, errors and latency

Fictional order-prediction lab; all data and runtime observations are authored fixtures. No credentials, live cloud resources or pullable container images are supplied. The image identities are computed from the included release package bytes. A deployment-capable authorized runtime must bind these fixture identities to its local image/scaffold; these files do not claim deployment occurred.

## Supplied contract
Anonymous feature_1 and feature_2, request key features, output keys predictions and version. These concrete names and limits are authored here because the glossary leaves them unnamed. Read contract.json before using any fixtures.

## Learner task (glossary)
Instrument one prediction handler in the supplied service scaffolding using learner-written imports and a learner-defined Python function. Include JSON decoding, prediction and JSON response encoding in handler timing, and record timestamped durations and status/error counts on successful and handled-error paths. Calculate handler latency mean and population standard deviation. Run the supplied external probe and fault scaffolding without implementing infrastructure or probe scheduling. Summarize all 300 client-side attempt outcomes and reconcile them with handler records.

## Starter-state intent (glossary)
Provide the existing single prediction handler, its valid request and response contract, the supplied prediction function, and empty handler telemetry collections. Supply the external probe, its client-side outcome record, and connection-refusal and response-timeout fault controls. Preserve the existing running-example request and response names; leave handler instrumentation and the result summary for the learner.

## Observable success (glossary)
Executing the supplied fixture produces handler duration and status/error records, including handled errors. The summary preserves all 300 external attempts, applies response validity and deadline checks, computes availability with denominator 300, calculates handler latency mean and population standard deviation, and explains external failures with no corresponding handler record without discarding those attempts.

## Visual intent (glossary)
Make external attempt outcomes and corresponding handler records visible together, including attempt timestamps, response validity, deadline outcomes and durations with declared units. Expose connection-refused and timeout attempts with absent handler records, alongside the fixed window, availability numerator and denominator, handler status/error counts, and latency statistics.

Dataset CSV headers and all records are copied from the registry by the builder. Measurement records are observations, not computed summary answers. Offline infrastructure helpers supply transport/status bytes or recorded outcomes; author the requested imports, logic, fixtures and assertions in learner.py. Runtime commands listed by the glossary are tasks for the authorized fixture environment, not commands this registry builder executes.

## Runnable uninstrumented handler and faults
Start `python3 endpoint_scaffold.py --fault none`; POST `http://127.0.0.1:8080/predict`. Stop with Ctrl-C before changing controls. `--fault handled_error` exercises the handled-error path; `--fault timeout` delays before handler dispatch beyond the contract deadline; `--fault connection_refusal` exits without listening (ensure no other process owns port 8080). Import and instrument `prediction_handler.handle_prediction`; timing, handler-event recording, summary and assertions remain learner work. `fixture_api.external_probe()` returns only the prescribed 300 baseline probe observations, not new measurements of the local service.

# Load-test a prediction endpoint against tail-latency and sustainable-throughput objectives

Fictional order-prediction lab; all data and runtime observations are authored fixtures. No credentials, live cloud resources or pullable container images are supplied. The image identities are computed from the included release package bytes. The executable offline runtime below binds fixture identities to the supplied local prediction packages; it does not claim real Docker/cloud deployment occurred.

## Supplied contract
Anonymous feature_1 and feature_2, request key features, output keys predictions and version. These concrete names and limits are authored here because the glossary leaves them unnamed. Read contract.json before using any fixtures.

## Learner task (glossary)
Run and inspect the supplied prediction-service image with its declared published HTTP port and nonsecret runtime settings. Author reusable valid, boundary and malformed JSON fixtures with assertions for the declared contract, keeping intentional rejection checks separate from capacity measurements. Use the supplied bounded load driver to exercise a small fixed range of offered rates with the stated valid payload mix, arrival/concurrency profile, warm-up and measurement duration. Account for outcomes, calculate completed-response latency statistics and successful throughput, inspect backlog throughout each window, and determine the measured feasible envelope against predeclared requirements.

## Starter-state intent (glossary)
Provide the referenced service image, declared port and nonsecret settings, existing prediction request/response contract, representative valid fixtures using only that contract's fields, boundary expectations and malformed-request expectations. Supply a bounded load driver that records client-visible outcomes, elapsed measurement time, completed-response latencies and backlog observations. Leave fixture assertions, metric calculations and acceptance decisions for the learner, with the fixed offered-rate range, warm-up, duration, timeout and acceptance limits already stated.

## Observable success (glossary)
Fixture assertions pass outside the capacity run. Every load report retains failures and timeouts, distinguishes offered rate from successful completed throughput, identifies the completed-latency sample and tracks unfinished work throughout the window. Calculated metrics and pass/fail decisions match the recorded observations and declared limits. The envelope result selects the greatest measured successful throughput among stable passing loads, or states that none passed.

## Visual intent (glossary)
Make each fixed offered load's duration, attempted requests, successful completions, separate failure counts, unfinished work and backlog trend visible alongside successful throughput, success probability, failed-request fraction, completed-response latency statistics and acceptance decision. Mark the highest measured successful throughput among stable passing loads, or show that no measured load qualifies.

Dataset CSV headers and all records are copied from the registry by the builder. Measurement records are observations, not computed summary answers. Offline infrastructure helpers supply transport/status bytes or recorded outcomes; author the requested imports, logic, fixtures and assertions in learner.py. Runtime commands listed by the glossary are tasks for the authorized fixture environment, not commands this registry builder executes.

## Executable OFFLINE authorized runtime
Run from this workspace. PyYAML is the declared configuration dependency (`import yaml`). Export the runtime secret variable named in runtime_contract.json from an authorized local secret source; no secret literal is supplied or written into configuration/state. Child services inherit this variable only.
1. `python3 offline_runtime.py init` initializes the isolated fixture state (rollback starts only B; worker/scaling start original_config.json; other concepts leave deployment actions to the learner).
2. `python3 offline_runtime.py serve` launches the supplied local endpoint at the HOST_PORT in runtime_contract.json. Use `--name`, `--image`, `--port`, `--case` or `--fault` to select supplied identities/controls. Do not launch a second server on an occupied port.
3. Prefix the concept's declared runtime command with `python3 offline_runtime.py exec`, for example `python3 offline_runtime.py exec docker inspect prediction`. Docker/Compose commands launch and inspect local services; image inspect resolves only fixture release identities. Compose reads the learner's YAML and applies its image/environment/ports/replicas/resources. Replicas use adjacent local host ports. Instance/SSH, autoscaling and repository operations are explicitly simulated local state transitions, never external operations or mutations of the pack repository. Use only commands permitted by constraints.json.
4. `python3 offline_runtime.py state` inspects scoped identity/configuration and configured-healthcheck State.Health; `python3 offline_runtime.py events` shows captured application/inspection/lifecycle ordering. `python3 offline_runtime.py cleanup` terminates only this fixture's child services when finished (harness cleanup, not a learner command).
POST and GET routes are prediction_route and readiness_route from contract.json on `http://127.0.0.1:<HOST_PORT>`. Request timeout is the contract's two seconds. This runtime produces local execution evidence, not production performance measurements. Learner configuration, acceptance assertions, measurements, readiness/authentication logic and verification decisions remain unwritten.

The offline runtime itself needs only standard-library Python on Linux. When PyYAML is unavailable to the harness, its private offline_yaml.py accepts the declared simple mapping/list/scalar configuration subset (including JSON-form YAML). Unsupported YAML forms are explicitly rejected. Learner yaml.safe_dump/yaml.safe_load work still requires the declared PyYAML dependency; the private parser is infrastructure, not a learner solution.

State.Health reports execution of the configured healthcheck, not an unconditional readiness probe.

# Choose inference batching under latency constraints

Fictional order-prediction lab; all data and runtime observations are authored fixtures. No credentials, live cloud resources or pullable container images are supplied. The image identities are computed from the included release package bytes. A deployment-capable authorized runtime must bind these fixture identities to its local image/scaffold; these files do not claim deployment occurred.

## Supplied contract

# Configure bounded prediction-worker concurrency on an existing runtime

Fictional order-prediction lab; all data and runtime observations are authored fixtures. No credentials, live cloud resources or pullable container images are supplied. The image identities are computed from the included release package bytes. The executable offline runtime below binds fixture identities to the supplied local prediction packages; it does not claim real Docker/cloud deployment occurred.

## Supplied contract
Anonymous feature_1 and feature_2, request key features, output keys predictions and version. These concrete names and limits are authored here because the glossary leaves them unnamed. Read contract.json before using any fixtures.

## Learner task (glossary)
Configure the approved limit of two workers for the supplied containerized runtime. Write and reload its Compose YAML safely, validate the resolved runtime contract, apply the supplied immutable image, and inspect worker processes and CPU/memory usage during the supplied load fixture.

## Starter-state intent (glossary)
Provide a mapping/list configuration containing only the supplied service name, immutable image reference, HOST:CONTAINER port mappings and declared nonsecret environment keys, including the existing worker-limit key. Supply CONFIG_PATH, NAME, the authorized load fixture and the worker-process identification guidance. Leave the worker-limit edit, safe YAML round-trip and runtime verification for the learner.

## Observable success (glossary)
The saved configuration safely reloads with the worker limit equal to two, and Compose validation resolves the intended contract. Container inspection confirms the supplied runtime is running. During the supplied load interval, worker-process evidence and CPU/memory measurements are recorded together; the observed worker count is compared with two and any oversubscription is explicitly reported.

## Visual intent (glossary)
Make the authored worker limit, safely reloaded value, Compose-resolved value and observed worker-process count visible together, alongside CPU/memory measurements from the same load interval. Distinguish worker processes from supporting processes and highlight any count above the illustrative limit of two.

Dataset CSV headers and all records are copied from the registry by the builder. Measurement records are observations, not computed summary answers. Offline infrastructure helpers supply transport/status bytes or recorded outcomes; author the requested imports, logic, fixtures and assertions in learner.py. Runtime commands listed by the glossary are tasks for the authorized fixture environment, not commands this registry builder executes.

## Executable OFFLINE authorized runtime
Run from this workspace. PyYAML is the declared configuration dependency (`import yaml`). Export the runtime secret variable named in runtime_contract.json from an authorized local secret source; no secret literal is supplied or written into configuration/state. Child services inherit this variable only.
1. `python3 offline_runtime.py init` initializes the isolated fixture state (rollback starts only B; worker/scaling start original_config.json; other concepts leave deployment actions to the learner).
2. `python3 offline_runtime.py serve` launches the supplied local endpoint at the HOST_PORT in runtime_contract.json. Use `--name`, `--image`, `--port`, `--case` or `--fault` to select supplied identities/controls. Do not launch a second server on an occupied port.
3. Prefix the concept's declared runtime command with `python3 offline_runtime.py exec`, for example `python3 offline_runtime.py exec docker inspect prediction`. Docker/Compose commands launch and inspect local services; image inspect resolves only fixture release identities. Compose reads the learner's YAML and applies its image/environment/ports/replicas/resources. Replicas use adjacent local host ports. Instance/SSH, autoscaling and repository operations are explicitly simulated local state transitions, never external operations or mutations of the pack repository. Use only commands permitted by constraints.json.
4. `python3 offline_runtime.py state` inspects scoped identity/configuration and configured-healthcheck State.Health; `python3 offline_runtime.py events` shows captured application/inspection/lifecycle ordering. `python3 offline_runtime.py cleanup` terminates only this fixture's child services when finished (harness cleanup, not a learner command).
POST and GET routes are prediction_route and readiness_route from contract.json on `http://127.0.0.1:<HOST_PORT>`. Request timeout is the contract's two seconds. This runtime produces local execution evidence, not production performance measurements. Learner configuration, acceptance assertions, measurements, readiness/authentication logic and verification decisions remain unwritten.

Worker execution controls: the supplied server honors the existing worker-limit environment variable by creating that many local worker processes. `python3 offline_runtime.py exec docker container top prediction` returns actual local supervisor/worker PIDs and the configured environment value. `python3 offline_runtime.py exec docker container stats prediction` samples local CPU and memory from /proc during the client-driven load and records the observation alongside elapsed time. The mounted CSV snapshots remain separately labeled authored observations, not outputs from this local run. Learner YAML edits, worker identification/count comparisons and oversubscription assertions remain unwritten.

The offline runtime itself needs only standard-library Python on Linux. When PyYAML is unavailable to the harness, its private offline_yaml.py accepts the declared simple mapping/list/scalar configuration subset (including JSON-form YAML). Unsupported YAML forms are explicitly rejected. Learner yaml.safe_dump/yaml.safe_load work still requires the declared PyYAML dependency; the private parser is infrastructure, not a learner solution.

State.Health reports execution of the configured healthcheck, not an unconditional readiness probe.

# Configure replica scaling to right-size serving capacity under a service objective

Fictional order-prediction lab; all data and runtime observations are authored fixtures. No credentials, live cloud resources or pullable container images are supplied. The image identities are computed from the included release package bytes. The executable offline runtime below binds fixture identities to the supplied local prediction packages; it does not claim real Docker/cloud deployment occurred.

## Supplied contract
Anonymous feature_1 and feature_2, request key features, output keys predictions and version. These concrete names and limits are authored here because the glossary leaves them unnamed. Read contract.json before using any fixtures.

## Learner task (glossary)
Configure the supplied nonproduction runtime from demand/capacity evidence. Calculate the declared mean and standard deviation, select bounded replica settings against the service objective, edit and safely reload its YAML configuration, and inspect resolved fields before applying it. Inspect running containers and instance identity/status before and after the authorized bounded demand and lifecycle actions, then restore the original replica and lifecycle settings.

## Starter-state intent (glossary)
Provide the existing authorized nonproduction runtime, its original YAML mapping/list configuration and replica/lifecycle settings, supplied demand/capacity observations as numeric_values, and completed_latency_values with declared_percentile. Include the existing SERVICE and INSTANCE/ZONE identifiers, supported scaling policy, measurement evidence, service objective, permitted bounds, and supplied controls for the bounded demand change, authorized lifecycle action and restoration.

## Observable success (glossary)
Saved evidence contains mean and standard deviation calculations, correctly defined service measurements, safely reloaded YAML fields, intended versus observed replica counts and identities, instance status and identity before and after the authorized action, and confirmation that the original replica and lifecycle settings were restored.

## Visual intent (glossary)
Make the original, changed and restored replica settings visible alongside resolved YAML bounds, observed container counts and identities, instance status and identity, and service measurements at the same declared load.

Dataset CSV headers and all records are copied from the registry by the builder. Measurement records are observations, not computed summary answers. Offline infrastructure helpers supply transport/status bytes or recorded outcomes; author the requested imports, logic, fixtures and assertions in learner.py. Runtime commands listed by the glossary are tasks for the authorized fixture environment, not commands this registry builder executes.

## Executable OFFLINE authorized runtime
Run from this workspace. PyYAML is the declared configuration dependency (`import yaml`). Export the runtime secret variable named in runtime_contract.json from an authorized local secret source; no secret literal is supplied or written into configuration/state. Child services inherit this variable only.
1. `python3 offline_runtime.py init` initializes the isolated fixture state (rollback starts only B; worker/scaling start original_config.json; other concepts leave deployment actions to the learner).
2. `python3 offline_runtime.py serve` launches the supplied local endpoint at the HOST_PORT in runtime_contract.json. Use `--name`, `--image`, `--port`, `--case` or `--fault` to select supplied identities/controls. Do not launch a second server on an occupied port.
3. Prefix the concept's declared runtime command with `python3 offline_runtime.py exec`, for example `python3 offline_runtime.py exec docker inspect prediction`. Docker/Compose commands launch and inspect local services; image inspect resolves only fixture release identities. Compose reads the learner's YAML and applies its image/environment/ports/replicas/resources. Replicas use adjacent local host ports. Instance/SSH, autoscaling and repository operations are explicitly simulated local state transitions, never external operations or mutations of the pack repository. Use only commands permitted by constraints.json.
4. `python3 offline_runtime.py state` inspects scoped identity/configuration and configured-healthcheck State.Health; `python3 offline_runtime.py events` shows captured application/inspection/lifecycle ordering. `python3 offline_runtime.py cleanup` terminates only this fixture's child services when finished (harness cleanup, not a learner command).
POST and GET routes are prediction_route and readiness_route from contract.json on `http://127.0.0.1:<HOST_PORT>`. Request timeout is the contract's two seconds. This runtime produces local execution evidence, not production performance measurements. Learner configuration, acceptance assertions, measurements, readiness/authentication logic and verification decisions remain unwritten.

The offline runtime itself needs only standard-library Python on Linux. When PyYAML is unavailable to the harness, its private offline_yaml.py accepts the declared simple mapping/list/scalar configuration subset (including JSON-form YAML). Unsupported YAML forms are explicitly rejected. Learner yaml.safe_dump/yaml.safe_load work still requires the declared PyYAML dependency; the private parser is infrastructure, not a learner solution.

State.Health reports execution of the configured healthcheck, not an unconditional readiness probe.

# Roll back a serving release to a previous approved registry artifact

Fictional order-prediction lab; all data and runtime observations are authored fixtures. No credentials, live cloud resources or pullable container images are supplied. The image identities are computed from the included release package bytes. The executable offline runtime below binds fixture identities to the supplied local prediction packages; it does not claim real Docker/cloud deployment occurred.

## Supplied contract
Anonymous feature_1 and feature_2, request key features, output keys predictions and version. These concrete names and limits are authored here because the glossary leaves them unnamed. Read contract.json before using any fixtures.

## Learner task (glossary)
Restore approved version A using its recorded immutable image reference on the supplied authorized runtime while faulty test version B remains running. Use runtime-injected credentials, the required environment and a distinct published HTTP port. Inspect A's container identity, State, available Health and logs; verify readiness and the bounded JSON prediction/version fixture before stopping and removing only B. Do not retrain or change model identity.

## Starter-state intent (glossary)
Supply faulty test version B already running, the approval record and immutable image reference for version A, and an authorized identity with runtime-injected credentials. Supply A's distinct container identity, required nonsecret environment, available published port, readiness and prediction endpoint contracts, and a bounded prediction fixture with expected version and prediction. Leave A unstarted and B intact.

## Observable success (glossary)
Runtime inspection identifies A's intended image and running State, with Health checked when configured. Sanitized log evidence contains no initialization or execution failures. Readiness and prediction calls return the expected status and payload within stated timeouts; JSON decoding precedes field assertions. A remains running, and the execution sequence shows B stopped and removed only after these checks pass.

## Visual intent (glossary)
Make the release transition and its ordering visible: B initially running; A started under a distinct identity using its approved immutable image; A's State, available Health, sanitized logs and decoded readiness/prediction evidence verified; then B stopped and removed while A remains active.

Dataset CSV headers and all records are copied from the registry by the builder. Measurement records are observations, not computed summary answers. Offline infrastructure helpers supply transport/status bytes or recorded outcomes; author the requested imports, logic, fixtures and assertions in learner.py. Runtime commands listed by the glossary are tasks for the authorized fixture environment, not commands this registry builder executes.

## Executable OFFLINE authorized runtime
Run from this workspace. PyYAML is the declared configuration dependency (`import yaml`). Export the runtime secret variable named in runtime_contract.json from an authorized local secret source; no secret literal is supplied or written into configuration/state. Child services inherit this variable only.
1. `python3 offline_runtime.py init` initializes the isolated fixture state (rollback starts only B; worker/scaling start original_config.json; other concepts leave deployment actions to the learner).
2. `python3 offline_runtime.py serve` launches the supplied local endpoint at the HOST_PORT in runtime_contract.json. Use `--name`, `--image`, `--port`, `--case` or `--fault` to select supplied identities/controls. Do not launch a second server on an occupied port.
3. Prefix the concept's declared runtime command with `python3 offline_runtime.py exec`, for example `python3 offline_runtime.py exec docker inspect prediction`. Docker/Compose commands launch and inspect local services; image inspect resolves only fixture release identities. Compose reads the learner's YAML and applies its image/environment/ports/replicas/resources. Replicas use adjacent local host ports. Instance/SSH, autoscaling and repository operations are explicitly simulated local state transitions, never external operations or mutations of the pack repository. Use only commands permitted by constraints.json.
4. `python3 offline_runtime.py state` inspects scoped identity/configuration and configured-healthcheck State.Health; `python3 offline_runtime.py events` shows captured application/inspection/lifecycle ordering. `python3 offline_runtime.py cleanup` terminates only this fixture's child services when finished (harness cleanup, not a learner command).
POST and GET routes are prediction_route and readiness_route from contract.json on `http://127.0.0.1:<HOST_PORT>`. Request timeout is the contract's two seconds. This runtime produces local execution evidence, not production performance measurements. Learner configuration, acceptance assertions, measurements, readiness/authentication logic and verification decisions remain unwritten.

Rollback startup: `python3 offline_runtime.py init` leaves B running on its release-record port and A unstarted. Run the declared docker run command via the exec prefix using rollback_contract.json values and replacement published port 8081:8080. A client URL is `http://127.0.0.1:8081`; container port remains 8080. Inspect/log/call and verify A before issuing stop/rm for prediction-B. runtime_observations.json contains separate expected initial-B and verified-A evidence, not automatic acceptance. Actual command evidence is offline_runtime.py events. B injects HTTP 500 fixture_release_fault after prediction execution; its package intentionally matches A.

The offline runtime itself needs only standard-library Python on Linux. When PyYAML is unavailable to the harness, its private offline_yaml.py accepts the declared simple mapping/list/scalar configuration subset (including JSON-form YAML). Unsupported YAML forms are explicitly rejected. Learner yaml.safe_dump/yaml.safe_load work still requires the declared PyYAML dependency; the private parser is infrastructure, not a learner solution.

State.Health reports execution of the configured healthcheck, not an unconditional readiness probe.
